system: You are a security investigator reviewing an alert. Base every claim only on the evidence available to you. Cite the record IDs that support each observation.

supporting_observations.claim: A process named pfupdater.exe ran from Leo Martins's AppData\Roaming\PixelForge directory, rather than the approved PixelForge updater location under Program Files.

That process connected through the proxy to updates.pixelforge-suite.co. The inventory identifies updates.pixelforge-suite.com as the approved update host, so the observed hostname differs by its top-level domain.
The same process made repeated connections to the .co hostname at approximately five-minute intervals: 13:37:36, 13:42:43, 13:47:14, 13:52:45, 13:57:44, 14:02:11, and 14:07:36 UTC.
Sysmon recorded a file-creation event targeting the same pfupdater.exe path while that process was running; the record alone does not establish whether the file's contents changed.

Dropbox and Google Drive File Stream launched in Leo Martins's user session. These services are not among the organization's approved file-sharing or cloud-storage services, though the records do not show them transferring data.

known_telemetry_limitations: The updater connections are recorded as HTTPS proxy CONNECT tunnels; the provided records show destination host, timing, and byte counts, but not the encrypted application content or downloaded files (T045-00089, T045-00112, T045-00137, T045-00166, T045-00184, T045-00191, T045-00235).
The available records do not provide a hash, digital-signature result, or file contents for the AppData\Roaming\PixelForge\pfupdater.exe executable (T045-00087, T045-00088).
The Dropbox and Google Drive records show process launches, not network connections or file-transfer activity (T045-00057, T045-00062).
claims_not_established: Whether pfupdater.exe is an authentic PixelForge binary, a modified binary, or an unrelated program using that name.
Whether the repeated HTTPS sessions downloaded or executed a payload, or transmitted sensitive data.
Whether Dropbox or Google Drive transferred organizational data during the review window.
Whether the file-creation event changed or replaced the updater executable.
additional_evidence_needed: Acquire and analyze the updater executable, including its hash, digital signature, origin, and file-system metadata.
Obtain proxy TLS inspection or endpoint network/content telemetry for the updater connections, including certificate details and any downloaded objects.
Review endpoint file and process activity around the updater's connections for child processes, persistence changes, or file modifications.
Check endpoint and cloud-service audit records for Dropbox or Google Drive synchronization and possible data transfer.
